Reporting a security problem

How to tell TSX-MR about a weakness in Dukan ERP or this website, and what we ask of you while you look.

Version 1.0 (draft) · Effective date not set

On this page

  1. How to report
  2. What we ask of you
  3. What happens next
  4. Not a security report

How to report

Write to security@preview.invalid. Please include what you found, where, the steps that reproduce it, and what someone could do with it. One problem per message helps.

Do not put another person’s personal information in your report. If you came across some, say so and describe it without copying it.

What we ask of you

  • Use only accounts and businesses that are yours, or that you have been allowed to test. Never sign in as someone else.
  • Do not read, copy, change or delete the information of a business or a person. If a test reaches such information, stop and report it.
  • Do not slow down, overload or interrupt the service, and do not send messages to people through it.
  • Do not try to trick staff or users, and do not test physical premises.
  • Give us a reasonable time to fix a problem before you tell anyone else about it.
  • Never ask for payment in exchange for not publishing or not exploiting what you found.

What happens next

TSX-MR reads every report sent to security@preview.invalid, replies to the address it came from, and tells you when the problem is fixed. TSX-MR does not offer payment or rewards for reports.

Whether TSX-MR undertakes not to take legal action against research done in good faith and within these rules is legal wording still to be approved. Pending decision: legal_review

Not a security report

A lost phone, a forgotten password or a sign-in problem is a support question: see the support page. To stop a lost phone from using your account, sign in on another phone and sign that device out under More → Devices.
